messages:
maria: Heads up — we need a fastpatch release for SDKs to fix the streaming header bug before the EOD change window (17:00 PT). Targets: @sam (py) and @jess (ts). Can we coordinate publishes, pinning, and a short rollback plan? I'll open the release PRs now.

sam: I have the Python wheel built and tests passing. Thinking of publishing as 0.9.1.post1 to avoid index conflicts. Will push artifacts once we agree on tagging.

jess: TS side is ready for 0.12.3-hotfix. Proposal: publish under a temporary dist-tag `canary-hotfix`, smoke for 30m, then promote to `latest` if green.

olga: Suggestion: pin the legacy sync client as `-legacy` for one week in the changelog + add deprecation note. For Dedicated customers we should include pinning instructions in release notes.

maria: Agreed on pinning. @release-bot can you queue a canary publish and run the smoke script? Also please attach the artifact urls for tracing.

release-bot: release-bot: Deploy job queued: repo=redwood-sdk, branch=hotfix/stream-header, steps=[build, test, canary-publish, smoke], queued_by=maria, ETA~8m.

leo: Smoke script I'll run once canary is published — runs streaming e2e with header spoofing and checks for dropped frames.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: npm publish started for @redwood/sdk@0.12.3-hotfix -> publishing to dist-tag `canary-hotfix`. Artifact sha256: a3f9...

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: npm publish succeeded. dist-tag: canary-hotfix. Python wheel uploaded to test.pypi; awaiting twine upload to pypi.

sam: twine upload to pypi complete — python package 0.9.1.post1 is live. Note: pip doesn't allow full unpublish; will prepare follow-up if we need to yank.

jess: Running smoke now against staging: streaming tests, auth header variations, and quick perf checks.

leo: Smoke checks: all green. No header drops, throughput normal. Observability shows no new error spikes.

maria: :thumbsup: Hold for 30m as planned. If errors crop up within 30m we rollback. Rollback plan summary in case: 1) remove npm dist-tag and re-point `latest` back to 0.12.2, 2) publish a corrective py post-release (0.9.2.post1) and instruct customers to pin, 3) update changelog + send customer notice.

olga: I'll prepare a small rollback script. Example: 
```
# rollback steps (manual, run by oncall)
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk 0.12.3-hotfix --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@0.12.2 latest
# For pip: publish a yanked patch and update docs to pin
# Note: PyPI doesn't support unpublish for older releases, use yanked metadata + post release
```

sam: Confirmed. Because pip unpublish is restricted we'll push 0.9.2.post1 with the corrective change and add a yanked marker in release notes. Also update the quickstart snippets to lock to 0.9.0 if needed.

jess: Promoting now: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@0.12.3-hotfix latest`

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: npm dist-tag add succeeded. @redwood/sdk@0.12.3-hotfix is now tagged as `latest`.

maria: OK — promote complete. I'll notify #marketing with the release note draft and remind them about the pinning guidance for Dedicated customers. Also add an entry to the deprecation tracker about the sync client pin.

olga: Added DEPRECATION-221 to the tracker and scheduled a follow-up reminder in 7 days. Drafted the pin instructions for customers (steps to set dependency to `@redwood/sdk@0.12.2-legacy` or pip equivalent).

jess: Final check: client SDK telemetry looks normal, no error rate uptick.

maria: Great work all. Post-release tasks: 1) update console changelog, 2) send customer-facing notes, 3) file a short postmortem if we see any regressions. I'm leaving this thread open for any late issues within the next 2 hours.

leo: I'll keep an eye on the streaming jobs dashboard for 2 hours.

sam: I'll draft the pip advisory note and push to the docs repo.

maria: Closing in 2h if no issues. Thanks :shipit:
